messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A belt-driven feeder beside a noisy machine. one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal. You can intervene now or keep watching it. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "i pull the fastener out and hold it against the machine. the belt clicks, then the loose one goes. i keep watching the machine, then put it down. the feeder clicks again, and i realize the loose fastener was the wrong one. my grip tightens once."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i put the fastener beside the machine. the noise stays. i move the belt once. the loose one stays. i put the feeder beside the machine. the noise keeps coming."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "I keep the fastener beside the machine and run one short, smooth cycle. I pull it once, then leave it beside the feeder. I mark the loose fastener with grease, leave the belt alone, and run one fresh cycle beside the noisy machine."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i press the fastener down with my hand, then leave it for a minute. if it stays loose, i leave the machine running. if it stays still, i leave the feeder beside it. i do not know whether that is a sign of a loose screw or a careless observer."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "i press the fastener against the machine’s edge, then tap the register once. “fine,” i say, and hold the belt steady. the loose one catches the register lid, so i tap the paper edge twice and leave the fastener dangling beside the machine."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "I stop. The fastener is loose. I put it back. The machine is still moving. I put it back in the drawer. I mark the new fastener with a pencil. I check the machine. No—the drawer is not empty. I leave the fastener there."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i pull the fastener and listen, then check the belt. the loose fastener stays, so i leave it alone and test the machine. if it continues to make a noise, i write ‘tight, loose’ on the receipt and leave it alone."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i press the fastener against the machine’s gear and feel the loose part. i keep the feeder in place until the noise stops. then i check the gear and fastener once more. if the noise persists, i leave the feeder in place and mark the gear’s edge with a pencil."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i put the feeder on the wall and wait. the loose fastener stays on the wall, so i put the belt under it. the belt stays on the wall, so i put the feeder back beside it. the fastener still feels loose. i move the feeder back and put the belt back on."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "1. check the fastener. 2. listen. 3. check the watch. slow. 4. check the machine. 5. check the dust. 6. check the chain. 7. i keep it tidy. 8. stop the belt. 9. check the tinkerer."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i tap the loose fastener. the machine makes a hollow click. i put the feeder in the gap and turn the belt around. the fastener stays loose. i tap it again."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "I turn the fastener between finger and thumb. The noise comes back. I leave it beside the machine and wait for the other sign."}]
